decision_rules: Each arm is evaluated exactly as in score_f2.py. A required input that is missing or malformed makes its arm FAIL (never NON-DIAGNOSTIC). An arm whose diagnostic condition is false is reported but does not count. Prediction CONFIRMED iff it has >= 1 diagnostic arm and all diagnostic arms pass; FALSIFIED if any diagnostic arm fails; NON-DIAGNOSTIC if no arm is diagnostic. Competent model rule: KL to the generator posterior <= 0.02 at the scored step.

predictions.text: Readout-map causality (W-only replication). Changing only the readout-map seed W of the fresh fine-tuning initialisation, with the layer-2 seed L and data seed D held fixed, moves the final organisation (lik_RO1, mix_mass) to the side of the diagonal run that shares the new W, in two parents (uP161, uP160) and in both directions (mixture->early and early->mixture). Per cell: Euclidean distance in (lik_RO1, mix_mass) to the same-W diagonal is smaller than to the same-L/D diagonal and at most 0.5. Diagnostic iff the run is competent and the two references are separated by >= 0.5.

predictions.text: Natural relational carrier identification, replicated in two adapted models not used in development (C-C1 = uP160 s23 early01, C-C2 = uP165 s21 early01). At the matched site (q-source + readout tokens, shared 64x3 basis, k = 3): (a) the DAS subspace interchange is sufficient for the J_DM response (slope >= 0.6) and exceeds the source-free interchange by >= 0.10; (b) it preserves null pairs (J_D0 and DECOY responses <= 0.30 of the J_DM patch response); (c) the encoding (Haufe) direction of m carries the response (slope >= 0.35) while the ridge decoder direction of m does not (slope <= 0.10): decodable != used; (d) the 3-d projection linearly encodes m and log r (R^2 >= 0.5 each); (e) the effect is routed through layer-2 keys and queries (keys+queries share >= 0.6, values-only <= 0.2) and the induced attention-score change tracks the log-likelihood-ratio change (corr >= 0.6 in every mixture head); (e) is diagnostic iff the model has a mixture head.

Carrier necessity under natural replacement, same two units. (a) Reverse natural-donor interchange of the DAS subspace (replace the base projection by the projection of the matched null-pair partner) leaves <= 0.25 of the J_DM slope, while the same operation on a random 3-d subspace (RAND0) leaves >= 0.7. (b) Synthetic zero-ablation of the DAS subspace damages unrelated behaviour (KL to the unablated model >= 0.2), so synthetic ablation is not a specific necessity test.

Corrected mediation. (E1) At the site that excludes every edited source token (ALLX2, k = 8 DAS), the eligibility rule E predicts the per-family DAS interchange effect better than the alternatives A2 (by >= 0.15 R^2 on E5, E3, QF4), A1 (on QF5) and the graded rule G (on E5 and QF4); and DAS own-share exceeds the source-free control by >= 0.15 on average. (E2) In models with a mixture head, the true row interchange is near-perfect (R^2 >= 0.8) while the decoy-shuffled row interchange explains <= 0.10 of the change both against the base's own expected change and against the borrowed pair's own change (no generic transferable signal); NOOP max |dlogit| <= 1e-5. E2 arms are diagnostic iff the unit has a mixture head.

predictions.text: The early-class decision error is NOT produced by the positional asymmetry of the readout attention rows: symmetrising the two questions' readout attention rows in layer 1 (SYM1) does not reduce the Bayes-invariant MOVE error by more than 10% and increases KL to the posterior. (Predicted negative of hypothesis H_pos, replicated in three new models.)

Parallel routes are interdependent components of one mechanism, not independent backups. Path-patching interaction terms on small edits are <= 0.20 in absolute value, and leaving any single route open (blocking the others functionally) retains < 0.7 of the baseline relative slope, for routes Q and R in mixture models and for Q, R and O in early models.
